Q: How should source connectors handle rate limits, redirects and untrusted destinations?
A: A connector has to preserve both source correctness and network safety. Respect documented retry hints and apply bounded backoff with jitter under a total deadline. Validate allowed destinations and redirects, because an initially permitted URL may redirect toward a forbidden network resource. Source credentials should remain scoped to their intended host and operation. Record partial progress and failure explicitly; a rate-limited scan is not evidence that every unseen source was deleted. Bound response sizes before retaining untrusted bodies.
Why: A connector receives two successful pages then a rate limit. It should retain a resumable partial scan and avoid interpreting the absent remaining pages as an authoritative deletion list.
Risk: Retrying without a total budget can hold workers indefinitely.
Trade: Incremental checkpoints reduce repeated work but need an explicit completeness contract.
Try: Simulate a redirect, a retry-after response and an interrupted paginated scan.
